approach: Root cause: a file kept by hand as a mirror of a governing source (xtask/shard-timings.txt, docs/decisions.md, status::BUILD_PATHS against the CI athena-bin key, docs/ontology.toml against the docs it scans) is tested for its shape only, or checked late, so content that contradicts the source passes until the final verdict. Fix at the origin with one registry, crates/athena-core/src/mirrors.rs. Each entry names a mirror file, its source and a comparison rule, and pure rule functions compare content. Four rules: (a) shard-timings `--test` and `--lib` lines equal the units on disk; (b) docs/decisions.md starts with the exact bytes of its base version; (c) the CI athena-bin hashFiles globs and the BUILD_PATHS list parsed out of the work tree's crates/athena-core/src/status.rs cover each other both ways (real drift today, so BUILD_PATHS gains four roots); (d) docs/ontology.toml, which exists in the base, is checked for identifying lines in BRIEF.md and the term sources that no sense or excuse covers, through one shared walk moved out of crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs. Revision changes: (1) rule (d) is live, not skipped. The dependents entry is corrected, Source::Docs gets a defined watch set (docs/ontology.toml, BRIEF.md, and every file source listed in the parsed ontology, using the shared scanned_files), with a unit test and a loop test where a producer adds an uncovered '- Hermes: ...' line to BRIEF.md and is sent back. (2) The 'never charged with base drift' claim is withdrawn: the filter works per entry, so a producer who touches a watched file can be charged with drift already at the base. This is stated, tested with a named expected result, and justified: the unfiltered repo test would fail `cargo test` on that drift in any case, so an early send-back costs nothing extra. The before-handover call site is the producer loop's self-check in run/producer.rs, which runs after every producer report and before verification. A repo-level athena-cli test target runs the registry over the real files (all entries, no filter) and over a drifted fixture per entry, so a new entry is covered with no other edit. checks.rs stays unchanged (decision 9).

decisions.choice: 1. One registry REGISTRY: &[Mirror] with Mirror { name, mirror, source: Source, rule: Rule }. Source is Path | Globs | GitHead | Docs; Rule is TimingUnits | AppendOnly | HashFilesCover | OntologyTerms (no rule carries data copied from the running binary). check_entry(entry, root, base) wraps every inner finding in a Drift { mirror, message }. check_all(root, base, touched: Option<&[String]>) runs every entry whose mirror file exists; with Some(paths) it runs only entries where Mirror::watches(root, paths) is true. watches by Source: Path(p) = mirror or p in paths; Globs = mirror or any path matching a pattern (segment-wise matcher); GitHead = mirror only; Docs = docs/ontology.toml, BRIEF.md, or any file source of a term in the parsed ontology at root (decision ids skipped, same test as scanned_files); a file that does not parse watches only itself and BRIEF.md. is_athena_source(root) (setup.sh, xtask/shard-timings.txt and crates/athena-core/Cargo.toml all exist) gates the producer-loop use. Filter limit, stated: the filter is per entry, not per finding. A producer who touches any file an entry watches is charged with every finding of that entry, including drift already in the base. This is accepted because athena-cli --test mirrors runs the same entry unfiltered under the configured `cargo test --locked`, so drift in the base fails the job at verification anyway; the early send-back names the file and fix a stage sooner and costs no extra failure.
decisions.reason: The cause is that nothing makes a mirror declare how it is compared to its source. A registry makes the declaration the unit and the repo test iterates it. The gate keeps jobs on other repositories, which may have their own docs/decisions.md, from being forced to append-only. The touch filter keeps a producer that touched none of an entry's files from being charged with it. Critic finding 12: the 'never' claim was stronger than the design, so it is softened to the per-entry statement above and a loop test fixes the expected result (sent back once, message names the missing b.rs line).

rejected.option: One more one-off test per mirror, as the five jobs did
rejected.why: Fixes one instance and leaves the class.

rejected.option: Put the registry in xtask
rejected.why: xtask does not depend on athena-core, so it cannot reach the other mirrors' code, and xtask tests run in a heavy shard outside the producer loop.

rejected.option: Run the registry on every repository the producer works in
rejected.why: docs/decisions.md append-only is Athena's own convention, so other repositories would get false send-backs.

rejected.option: Run touched entries on the base tree too and report only new findings (critic finding 12 first option)
rejected.why: Needs a materialized base tree for the disk-scanning rules (units on disk, ontology scans); the snapshot git can read single files but not a tree walk, and the benefit is small because base drift also fails the unfiltered repo test. Softening the claim is the smaller design.

rejected.option: No touch filter at all
rejected.why: A producer that changed none of a mirror's files could be charged with an unrelated entry's drift.

decisions.choice: 2. Rule (c) reads BUILD_PATHS from the mirror file it names: status_build_paths(status_rs_text) finds `pub const BUILD_PATHS`, starts after the `=` (so the `[&str; 9]` type is skipped), reads to the next `;` and collects the quoted strings. hash_glob_problems(ci_text, roots) takes those roots. Mirror = crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, Source::Path(.github/workflows/ci.yml). (i) Each hashFiles glob on an `athena-bin-` key line must be covered by a root (a root ending `/` covers a glob starting with it, a file root its exact name); else the message says add the path to BUILD_PATHS in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs. (ii) Each root must be covered by a glob (a dir root needs a glob that starts with it and ends `**`); else it says add the glob to every athena-bin key. A ci.yml with no such key line, or a status.rs whose array cannot be parsed, is a drift. The athena-cli repo test asserts the parsed list equals the compiled status::BUILD_PATHS. BUILD_PATHS becomes nine roots: crates/, xtask/, rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh, docs/system-facts.md; stale_build_line prints the list from the constant.
decisions.reason: The rule must judge the files in the work tree, not the compiled constant of an installed binary that can be older than the tree. The drift is real: xtask/tests/policy.rs (lines 783, 897-1000) forces the key to equal xtask BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS (xtask/src/main.rs 267-277), the true input set; athena.toml is compiled in (athena-gate lib.rs 33 BUILTIN_CONFIG), docs/system-facts.md too (athena-context briefs.rs 1671 SYSTEM_FACTS) and rust-toolchain.toml changes the compiler, yet touches_build (status.rs 23-29) and stale_build_line (35-58) ignore them, so a landing that changes them leaves a stale binary. defaults.toml is an xtask build input; adding it costs at most an extra rebuild and keeps one rule with no excusal list.

rejected.option: Rule::HashFilesCover(&status::BUILD_PATHS), the compiled constant
rejected.why: Judges the work tree by the binary's older build; false and missed send-backs.

rejected.why: Leaves the producer's own edit of BUILD_PATHS or the key unchecked before handover; the parse is small and the repo test pins it to the constant.

rejected.why: A full parse for one array; the narrow parse plus the equality assertion is enough.

rejected.option: Excuse the four extra globs with reasons and leave BUILD_PATHS alone
rejected.why: The files are compiled in, so the installed binary really is stale after a change to them.

rejected.option: Edit ci.yml
rejected.why: Governance, out of scope, and the key is already the true input set.

decisions.choice: 3. Rule (d) shares the whole walk with the ontology test, and runs live on the real docs/ontology.toml. mirrors.rs gets plain-data types OntologyTerm { name, aliases, sources, senses (in_file, marker), excused } and pub fns is_word_char, phrase_in, names_term, is_identifying, Hit, scan, is_decision_id, names_of, scanned_files, term_hits, excuse_ok, uncovered_lines, parse_ontology(toml_text) (toml_edit, already an athena-core dependency) and ontology_problems(toml_text, read_file). The inner uncovered-line text from ontology.rs 413-430 ('{name}: {path}:{n} names the term as a definition or role and no sense or excuse covers it: {line}') is unchanged. check_entry wraps it in a Drift whose message starts with `docs/ontology.toml:` and ends with the fix `add a senses entry or an excuse for that term in docs/ontology.toml`. ontology.rs keeps its serde types and its sense/says and excuse-shape checks, converts each serde Term with plain() and calls the shared fns; a new test both_parsers_read_the_same_terms asserts plain(serde term) == parse_ontology(text) on the real file.
decisions.reason: Criterion 3 needs a mirrors unit test for 'term found in a governing doc but sense unlisted'; the logic cannot be tested in mirrors.rs without living there, and a second copy would be a new hand-kept mirror of the ontology logic. The file exists in the base (Glob: docs/ontology.toml; claim_problems at ontology.rs 312-433 already checks it under cargo test), so the entry runs for real in the repo test and in the producer loop; the registry adds the early, producer-side signal for the same check. The inner message names neither mirror nor fix, so the Drift wrapper supplies both.

rejected.why: A new hand-kept mirror of the ontology logic.

rejected.why: Changes Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock for one parser; --locked builds make it a larger change.

decisions.choice: 4. Rule (a) derives `--test` and `--lib` units from disk: crates/*/tests/*.rs, crates/*/tests/*/main.rs and xtask/tests (unit `<dir name> --test <stem>`), and crates/*/src/lib.rs (unit `<dir name> --lib`). missing_timing_lines(units, timings_text) reports a unit missing from the file and a `--test` or `--lib` line with no unit; `--doc` and `--bin` lines are never reported. The entry's Source::Globs lists those patterns. derived_units_agree_with_cargo_metadata runs `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 --locked` (as xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs does around line 120) and asserts the `--test` and `--lib` units of targets with test=true equal the derived set. `--doc` and `--bin` stay with the heavier oracle in ci_shards.rs (around line 420).
decisions.reason: A new crate's lib is as likely to be missed as a test file, and both are cheap facts on disk. The agreement test compares the derived copy with cargo's own answer. `--bin` names can be renamed (athena-cli's bin is `athena`) and `--doc` depends on the doctest flag, so deriving them would be a guess; the limit is stated.

rejected.option: Derive `--bin` and `--doc` units too
rejected.why: Needs Cargo.toml parsing; it re-creates cargo metadata.

rejected.option: Name the ci_shards test as the rule and only run it
rejected.why: Criterion 3 needs a unit test that fails on literal text; ci_shards runs in the heavy xtask lane.

rejected.option: Make xtask depend on athena-core
rejected.why: Changes xtask/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock and pulls a heavy crate into a CI-support crate.

decisions.choice: 5. Rule (b) append_only_problem(base: &[u8], new: &[u8]) fails unless base is a byte prefix of new, and names docs/decisions.md, the first changed line and the fix (append, do not edit). The base comes from an injected closure `&dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>`. The producer loop builds it only when `snapshot.base()` is Some(base) (Option<&str>, crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs line 131): `move |p| snapshot.git().show_file(base, p).ok().flatten()`; when base() is None the closure returns None, which skips rule (b). Git::show_file (athena-git lib.rs 453) takes &str and returns Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>. The repo test uses git_base(root) with HEAD; a None base skips the rule. crates/athena-cli/src/decisions.rs keeps its PINNED_LEN/PINNED_SHA256 test for committed history.
decisions.reason: This is the rag3 prevention. The producer's snapshot is a git repository whose base commit is the dispatch base, so the base text is readable while it edits.

rejected.option: Replace the pinned-hash test
rejected.why: It guards committed history, which a base comparison cannot.

rejected.option: Compare with origin/main
rejected.why: The snapshot has no remote.

decisions.choice: 6. The before-handover call site is the producer loop's existing self-check in crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs (after unmet/unchanged/gate/outside, lines 285-320). Add `let mirrors = if self.nested.is_none() && !changes.is_empty() { mirror_drift_in(&snapshot, &changed) } else { Vec::new() };` after the gate (line 306), add `&& mirrors.is_empty()` to the break condition (lines 313-318), push `files kept by hand disagree with their source: ...` into `problems` after the `report_problems` clone (line 343, as the gate does), print a ui line when a drift remains at the limit (near line 385) and break as the gate does. Apply `append_mirror_drift(text, &mirrors)` to the result of the `attempt_brief = match` (lines 407-423). In run/send_back.rs append_mirror_drift returns the text unchanged for an empty list; otherwise it puts one leading sentence before the text ('Files that are kept by hand disagree with the source they summarize; this is a reason for this send-back whether or not criteria are listed.') and appends a section listing each Drift message. mirror_drift_in returns an empty list unless mirrors::is_athena_source(snapshot.dir()), and calls check_all(dir, base, Some(&changed)). It shares the single PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS slot (line 374). A nested run is judged by the outer job.
decisions.reason: The mechanism the 'mechanism' default and criterion 5 ask for is an invocation, not a sentence. The loop runs before verification on the one-commit snapshot, so the base is readable. With drift alone the match falls to send_back_text, whose intro speaks only of unmet criteria, so the wrapper adds the leading sentence.

risks.risk: Changing BUILD_PATHS makes a landing that touches athena.toml, defaults.toml, rust-toolchain.toml or docs/system-facts.md trigger a rebuild in the drain, and a drain test that landed athena.toml (tests/drain.rs line 3117) may assert no rebuild.
risks.mitigation: This is the intended fix. The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` and changes only an expectation that asserted no rebuild, saying so in the report.

risks.risk: The loop hook sends back on drift already in the base: the filter is per entry, so a producer who edits any watched file (for example a lib.rs or a doc the ontology scans) is charged with that entry's pre-existing findings.
risks.mitigation: Stated in D158 and tested (loop test 4: base lacks the b.rs timing line, producer edits a.rs, sent back once with b.rs named). The same entry runs unfiltered in athena-cli --test mirrors under `cargo test --locked`, so base drift would fail the job at verification anyway. The real-repo test is run at base in step 5 and any drift there is fixed (true drift) or the rule corrected (false positive) first. The loop sends back once, then leaves with a ui line.

risks.risk: The live ontology entry sends back a producer who edits BRIEF.md or a term source doc and adds an identifying line (bullet, heading, table row) that names a term such as Hermes with no covering sense or excuse.
risks.mitigation: That is a true drift, the same one the ontology test reports under cargo test; the early message names the term, file, line and the fix (add a senses entry or an excuse in docs/ontology.toml). Matching is the moved, unchanged code, and the ontology tests (hermes_with_only_the_tool_sense_is_flagged_until_both_senses_are_listed and others) pin it. Base drift in the ontology is excluded by running the real-repo test at base first.

risks.risk: The touch filter is too narrow (a producer changes a source in a way Mirror::watches misses) so drift passes the loop.
risks.mitigation: The loop is the early signal only; the same registry runs unfiltered in athena-cli --test mirrors under the configured test check. Unit tests cover watches for each Source form, Docs included.

risks.risk: The registry runs on a repository that is not Athena's source and fails it.
risks.mitigation: is_athena_source gate, plus skip when a mirror file is absent; loop test 7 uses a repository without those files and asserts no send-back.

risks.risk: Moving the ontology walk changes ontology test behavior, or the two parsers (toml in the test, toml_edit in athena-core) diverge.
risks.mitigation: Functions move verbatim with messages unchanged; the existing ontology tests run; both_parsers_read_the_same_terms compares plain data of both parsers on the real file.

risks.risk: Derived `--test` and `--lib` units diverge from cargo's target set, for example a [[test]] with a custom path.
risks.mitigation: derived_units_agree_with_cargo_metadata on the real repo; on disagreement the producer fixes the derivation, not the timings file.

risks.risk: The narrow parse of BUILD_PATHS breaks if status.rs is reformatted.
risks.mitigation: Parse failure is itself a drift with a message, and the repo test asserts parsed == compiled constant.

risks.risk: The append-only rule compares with the base, so it is trivially true once committed and skipped with no git.
risks.mitigation: It bites on uncommitted edits, which is the producer's loop. The decisions.rs pin still guards committed history. D158 states the limit.

risks.risk: The drift shares the single send-back slot, so a producer already sent back for unmet criteria gets no second chance for drift.
risks.mitigation: Same as the gate today. The drift then stays and the configured `cargo test --locked` fails on athena-cli --test mirrors. D158 states this.

risks.risk: A future mirror is added but never registered, so the class returns.
risks.mitigation: The module doc and D158 say the registry is where a mirror is declared and mark registration prose-only. A new Rule variant without a fixture fails to compile in the repo test.

risks.risk: The producer's 'Planned files left unchanged' check flags checks.rs, which the reading lists.
risks.mitigation: The report explains it is unchanged because the hook moved to the producer loop (decision 9).

risks.risk: The shard-timings value for the new target is a guess.
risks.mitigation: The file header says values are estimates and the cover test checks names only; use 6.00, near the ontology target.
